items.item: No generated face, avatar or synthetic human in any frame
items.note: Thirty-six frames, one every ten seconds. Nothing but type, charts and the corner; no figure appears anywhere in the film.
No texture is used at all. Every frame is the paper room: a kinetic card, a chart, a figure, or a chapter card.

items.item: Every number on screen traces to a model run, and demo data is labelled
items.note: Every figure is drawn from facts.json and run.json through the reveal loop; nothing is typed into a scene. The TARNHOLLOW DEMO DATA chip is on every frame that carries a figure or a chart. The two chapter cards and the one kinetic beat with no figure in it carry no chip, which is right: there is no demo claim on them to label.

items.item: Charts are Manim scenes driven by engine output, not hand-rebuilt
items.note: Elasticity reads the run's own curve, points and band for TH-OVEMIT-22; SampleSize reads the fit's standard error and periods. Both are the scenes/ classes, in the site's chart grammar.

items.item: Every chart builds progressively and carries an annotation
items.note: Axes and labels, then the points, then the band, then the fit, then the annotations: the elasticity at the curve's end, the interval across the band, the three rungs on the error curve. The build is visible across f-006 to f-010 and f-018 to f-026.

items.item: Room tone, data ticks, transition SFX and a ducking bed
items.note: mix.json: room tone at -48 dB, six ticks, two whooshes, bed-elevenlabs.mp3 at -32 dB ducking to -20 dB. QA reads no silence over a second anywhere in the film.

items.item: A publishable voice, disclosed as what it is
items.note: voice is "library": the ElevenLabs library voice the founder chose on 2026-10-04 (content/assets/voice.json), which PREMIUM-STANDARD accepts as amended. The disclosure line it has to carry is the library one, and whether the description carries it is the describe step's check, not this one: qa.json reports disclosure_in_description as null because description.md does not exist yet.

items.item: Cut to VISUAL_SPEC §4, and nothing frozen over four seconds
items.note: qa.json: 46 cuts, mean interval 7.69 s, longest 24.57 s, inside the thirty a chart build may hold; no frozen run in any scene clip. Both of this step's first failures are fixed at the source rather than waived, and the fixes are in the engine, not in this film: the hold now measures a picture by how long it has been on screen, and the freeze check against a floor calibrated for ink on paper.

items.item: Subtitles burned in, legible, never boxed
items.note: Coverage 1.0, transcript match 0.982. Inter Display in ink with a thin paper outline, two lines, centred over a wide bottom margin; no box, no auto-caption look. The picture keeps out of the band on every frame.

items.item: The style lock is written and followed
items.note: content/assets/style-lock.json, locked from V01 on 2026-10-05. Paper #ffffff, ink, one blue, Inter Display at the stage's sizes; the chapter card is the spec's hairline and title with no numbering (f-017). Nothing in these frames departs from it.

items.item: One blue element per frame, and blue only on money and the leak
items.note: The only blue accents in the film are the spoken money figures ($65,320 at f-011 and f-014) and nothing else: the error curve, the rungs, every kinetic card and every other callout are ink. The elasticity band is the house Monte Carlo wash at 13% opacity, which BRAND.md names as the way a range is drawn and which the style lock carries as a token, so it is ground rather than a second accent. Worth the founder's eye at the final review all the same: a frame with the money figure over the band has blue in two places, even if only one of them is an element.

items.item: No gradient, glow, halo or vignette; hard cuts only
items.note: None in any frame. Transitions are hard cuts; the only motion inside a shot is the drift the spec asks for.

items.item: At most three text blocks per frame, captions small and dim
items.note: The busiest frames are the chart ones: heading, then at most two callouts in the right column, with the burned-in subtitle under them, which the standard counts separately. Callouts are capped at two by the style lock and the older of the pair steps back from blue to ink.

items.item: Charts have direct labels, a demo label, no legend and no grid
items.note: Hairline axes, three or four numbers on each, every line named where it sits. No legend and no gridlines anywhere.

This failed on the first pass and was fixed, not waived. Three defects, all in the chart scenes and all now re-rendered: the interval's low end, high end and width were drawn at one anchor and printed over each other into an unreadable smear (f-009, f-010), so the figure now replaces itself the way the paths' spread already did; the elasticity label was hung off the curve's last point and shifted back along it, so the fit ran through its glyphs (f-008), and it now sits above the band's end, clamped inside the plot; and a SKU code set at the callout's size ran off the right edge of the stage (f-006), so a figure wider than its column is now set smaller rather than over the edge.

notes: Fifteen items, all passing, after three legibility fixes to the chart scenes and the two cadence fixes the program checks caught. Nothing here is waived and nothing is judged by the frames alone where a program could judge it. One thing for the founder's eye at the final review: a frame carrying a blue money figure over the elasticity band has blue in two places, which the brand's own grammar allows (the band is the house wash for a range, not an accent) but which only he can settle for the series.
